page.layout: One column of running text with italic question headings set apart; no marginal notes. Printed page 460 at the head, running head "DE RUDIMENTIS" at the top centre.

main_text.p: alicujus, quia tunc ei, cujus eft, licet pifcari, & non aliis, Nam Ulpianus inquit: In laçu, qui mei domini eft, utique pifcari aliquem prohibere poffum. l. injuriarum in fine. ff. de injuriis & famof. libell.
Quæ in civitatibus funt, Theatra, ftadia & fiqua alia lunt civitatum communia. §. univerfitatis. inft. cod.
Nullius funt res facræ & religiofæ, & fanctæ: quod enim Divini juris eft, id nullius in bonis eft. §. nullius. inft. cod.

Sacræ res funt quæ ritè per pontifices Deo confecratæ funt: veluti ædes facræ, & donaria, quæ ritè ad minifterium Dei dedicata funt: quæ etiam alienari & obligari prohibuit Imperator, excepta caufa redemptionis captivorum. §. facræ res. inft. cod.
Religiofum locum unufquifque fua voluntate facit, dum mortuum infert in locum fuum. §. religiofum. inft. cod.

Sanctæ res veluti muri & portæ civitatis, quodammodo Divini juris funt: & ideo nullius in bonis funt. Ideo autem muros sanctos dicimus, quia pœna capitis constituta est in eos, qui aliquid in muros deliquerint. §. sanctæ quoq; inst. cod.
Singulorum hominum multis modis res fiunt: quarundam enim rerum dominiū nancifcimur jure naturali, quod ficut diximus appellatur jus gentiū: quarundam verò jure civili. §. singulorum. inst. cod.
Dominium est jus de re corporali perfectè dispo-nendi

page.notes: A dark ink stain lies beside the line "quoq; inst. cod." and is not text, so it is left out. The "s" in the printed "fanctæ" and "fanctos" is a long s; it is written as a plain s. Some headings are set in italic with the word "Dominium" in a larger capital; the text is copied as printed. The last paragraph breaks off mid-sentence at the foot of the page and continues on the next page.
